title: Complete Agentic AI Bootcamp With LangGraph and Langchain
_comment_title: §1 verbatim rule taken literally — the Udemy listing capitalises 'With' and writes 'Langchain' (no camel-case K). Earlier revision of this file silently 'corrected' both. The prose fields below use the vendor's own spelling 'LangChain'; only `title` is a copy.
_comment_overview: PARAPHRASED — never copy Udemy marketing prose verbatim. Facts (45.5h, 27 sections / 183 lectures, self-paced) are used as-is; the wording is rewritten.
overview: A self-paced, project-heavy bootcamp on building AI agents and multi-agent systems with LangGraph and LangChain. It runs from Python fundamentals through the LangChain retrieval stack and into production agentic patterns — ReAct agents, RAG variants, human-in-the-loop, MCP and deep agents. 45.5 hours of on-demand video across 27 sections, closing with four end-to-end agentic applications.
_comment_level: Genuinely spans both — the first ~45 lectures are Python syntax, Numpy/Pandas and Pydantic; the last are multi-agent MCP and deep-agent systems. `level` is the fusion_rank anchor (intermediate = safest single match point); `level_range` is stored for a future two-sided level_match term and is NOT scored today.
_comment_prereqs: Listing states requirements: basic Python (variables, functions, classes), basic REST/API familiarity, and conceptual familiarity with LLMs — no prior LangGraph. Those are generic entry conditions rather than a named catalog course, so `prereq_ids` stays empty; recording them here so a later curator doesn't read the empty array as 'not checked'.
_comment_price: Udemy price is coupon-driven (the source URL carries ?couponCode=KEEPLEARNING) and fluctuates with sales. DO NOT store a number — it would be wrong within days and generate would inject a stale price as fact. price_band 'low' is estimated from Udemy's typical discounted India range (₹500-₹4,000), not from an observed number; §2 requires that basis be recorded, and this is it.
price_note: Priced via Udemy, frequently discounted — check current price at checkout
_comment_platform: Unlike the krishnaikacademy.com courses (source_platform 'own_site'). Lets the card disclose the platform and lets external-platform courses be excluded from the owned-site upsell chain (D5) if that is ever restricted.

format._comment_duration: Two figures on one page: the 'This course includes' box says '45.5 hours on-demand video', the curriculum header says '27 sections • 183 lectures • 45h 40m total length' (=45.67h). Stored the includes-box figure; the 10-minute gap is listing rounding, not a version skew.
format._comment_dates: Neither a publish date nor a 'Last updated' badge was captured in the source dump. Left null rather than guessed — freshness.py scores unknown recency at the defined 0.35 floor (below the one-year mark), which is the honest outcome: this course must not out-rank a known-fresh one on an invented date. Udemy does publish 'Last updated' on the listing; capture it next pass and freshness rises on real evidence.
format._comment_curriculum_version: Udemy publishes no version string for this course. Null per §7 rather than inventing one — note that the syllabus does track LangChain v1 (a 'Langchain Updates V1' lecture plus the middleware lectures), so the content is post-v1.

_comment_rating: Star rating and review count were not present in the captured text — leave null, don't guess. validate_seed.py's null-rating warning is expected here.

_comment_objectives: §1 corroboration rule applied — nothing dropped. All four published objectives are supported by real lectures (ReAct architecture, agent memory/streaming, the multi-agent travel assistant, agentic RAG, MCP servers). The last two objectives are ADDED by curation, not published: the RAG-variant and human-in-the-loop/guardrails blocks are ~15 lectures of the syllabus and are the course's strongest differentiator, yet the marketing objectives never name them. They are corroborated by module_groups, which is the direction the rule cares about.
_comment_sections: The listing header says 27 sections / 183 lectures, but the captured dump preserved only a flat lecture list with no section headers. The ten groups below are a topic clustering of that flat list, i.e. an APPROXIMATION of the real section structure — deliberate under §4 (6-12 thematic chunks, never one chunk per lecture; 183 lecture vectors would starve the rest of the catalog out of RRF). Follow-up, non-blocking: copy the actual 27 section titles from the course page.
